title: The acceptable-numbering padding proof mixes standard and translated indices.
details: Marks, dated 2024-02-25, Theorem 6.11 proof, printed p. 34 (PDF page 34). In Case 2 the finite set B_k contains translated indices g(h(e,i)), which are indices for the numbering psi. The preceding argument shows psi_j is everywhere undefined for every j in B_k, and phi_e is everywhere undefined. The displayed definition of the standard program m instead tests m in B_k and infers a fact about phi_m from that membership; the translation identity only identifies phi_m with psi_(g(m)). Replace both tests in the definition of phi_m and the ensuing case analysis by g(m) in B_k. If that test held, phi_m would be constantly one while phi_m=psi_(g(m)) would be everywhere undefined, a contradiction. Thus g(m) is outside B_k and phi_m is everywhere undefined, hence equals phi_e, supplying the required new translated index. The nearby phrase psi_e should be phi_e. This repairs the specified Case 2 index mismatch; it is not a new audit of the subsequent isomorphism construction. The uniform-self-reference treatment adopts Definition 6.10 and Exercise 6.14, and excludes Theorem 6.11 and its proof.
